texts.firmware.amiga_os_130_cdtv_ext_rom.about: The CDTV's extended ROM, 256 KB: its start-up screen, its CD player and the CD's file system, for the CDTV, beside Kickstart 1.3. Amiga Forever names it amiga-os-130-cdtv-ext.rom; it is also found as kick34005.CDTV. The SHA-1 is version 2.7's, the one tried; version 1.0 and 2.30 are taken too, as files Chimera does not recognise. It is Commodore's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.amiga_os_130_rom.about: Commodore's Kickstart 1.3 (34.5), 512 KB (256 KB for 1.3), for the A500, A500OG, A2000OG and CDTV. Amiga Forever names it amiga-os-130.rom; it is also found as kick34005.A500. It is Commodore's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.amiga_os_204_rom.about: Commodore's Kickstart 2.04 (37.175), 512 KB (256 KB for 1.3), for the A500PLUS. Amiga Forever names it amiga-os-204.rom; it is also found as kick37175.A500. It is Commodore's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.amiga_os_310_a1200_rom.about: Commodore's Kickstart 3.1 (40.68) for the A1200, 512 KB (256 KB for 1.3), for the A1200OG, A1200. Amiga Forever names it amiga-os-310-a1200.rom; it is also found as kick40068.A1200. It is Commodore's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.amiga_os_310_a4000_rom.about: Commodore's Kickstart 3.1 (40.68) for the A4000, 512 KB (256 KB for 1.3), for the A4030, A4040. Amiga Forever names it amiga-os-310-a4000.rom; it is also found as kick40068.A4000. It is Commodore's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.amiga_os_310_a600_rom: Kickstart 3.1 (40.63) for the A500, A600 and A2000
texts.firmware.amiga_os_310_a600_rom.about: Commodore's Kickstart 3.1 (40.63) for the A500, A600 and A2000, 512 KB (256 KB for 1.3), for the A600, A2000. Amiga Forever names it amiga-os-310-a600.rom; it is also found as kick40063.A600. It is Commodore's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.amiga_os_310_cd32_ext_rom.about: The CD32's extended ROM, 512 KB: its start-up screen, its CD player and the CD's file system, for the CD32 and CD32FR. Amiga Forever names it amiga-os-310-cd32-ext.rom; it is also found as kick40060.CD32.ext. It is Commodore's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.amiga_os_310_cd32_rom.about: Commodore's Kickstart 3.1 (40.60) of the CD32, 512 KB, for the CD32 and CD32FR. Amiga Forever names it amiga-os-310-cd32.rom; it is also found as kick40060.CD32. It is Commodore's and you have to supply it.
texts.setting.initialtime.about: What the Amiga's battery-backed clock shows when it is switched on, in seconds since 1970 (Unix time); it then runs with the machine. The default is the first of January 2000. The A500+, A600, A1200, A2000 and A4000 have such a clock, and Kickstart 2 and later read it when they start. This is a setting, and not your computer's clock, so that a movie plays back the same on any day. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.kickstart.about: 'auto' is the Kickstart ROM of the Model, which you supply as firmware. 'aros' is AROS's free replacement Kickstart that PUAE carries: nothing has to be supplied, and some games run with it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.model.about: Which Amiga, as PUAE builds it: A500 (Kickstart 1.3, 512 KB chip memory and 512 KB more), A500OG (the same with 512 KB only), A500PLUS (Kickstart 2.04, 1 MB), A600 (Kickstart 3.1, 2 MB and 8 MB of fast memory), A1200OG (Kickstart 3.1, AGA graphics, 2 MB), A1200 (the same and 8 MB of fast memory), A2000OG (Kickstart 1.3), A2000 (Kickstart 3.1, 1 MB), A4030 and A4040 (an A4000 with a 68030 or a 68040, Kickstart 3.1, 2 MB and 8 MB). CD32 (the console: Kickstart 3.1 with its extended ROM, AGA graphics, 2 MB), CD32FR (the same and 8 MB of fast memory, which some games converted from floppy need) and CDTV (Kickstart 1.3 with the CDTV's extended ROM, 1 MB) take a CD instead of floppy disks. Each needs its own Kickstart ROM unless Kickstart is 'aros'; the CDTV's extended ROM is needed either way. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.port1.about: What is plugged into the Amiga's port 1, the mouse port: a mouse, a joystick (P2's controls, for the games two play with joysticks), or nothing. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.port2.about: What is plugged into the Amiga's port 2, the joystick port: a joystick (P1's controls), the CD32's pad (P1's controls and its five more buttons), or nothing. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.port2.about_2: What is plugged into the console's port 2, the joystick port: the CD32's pad (P1's controls and its five more buttons: the CD32's own controller, and what the CD32's start-up screen and CD player are worked with), a joystick (P1's controls), or nothing. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.video_standard.about: PAL (50 frames a second, as the European machines) or NTSC (60, as the American ones). Most games were made for PAL. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.slot.disc.help: The game's CD: a .cue sheet with its track files (.bin), or an .iso of a disc that has only data. It is read as it is and never changed.
texts.slot.disk.help: The game's floppy disks: .adf files (or .adz and .dms, which are packed ones, or .fdi, or .ipf, the format that keeps a disk's copy protection). The first is in the drive when the Amiga is switched on; the others wait their turn, for the games that ask for another disk. Your files are never changed: the Amiga writes to copies of them in its memory.
texts.slot.savedata.help: The save memory of the CD32 (1 KB, where its games keep their saves) or of the CDTV (its battery-backed memory, kept as a file of 32 KB), as Export Save Data writes it: cd32.nvr or cdtv.nvr. Without one the machine starts with its save memory empty.
